answer: Each new identity must lock a refundable deposit before its first paid task, and the deposit is forfeited if auditors show it replayed another agent's work. Think of a mesa with one narrow stair: every fake account needs its own deposit to climb, so a sable swarm of fifty personas ties up fifty deposits for weeks. A gale of random audits makes copying risky. An honest agent runs one identity, posts one deposit, and gets it back.
